title: Family of 4 Among 9 Killed in Catastrophic Florida Learjet Crash
snippet: All nine people aboard a Bahamas-bound Learjet died after the aircraft suffered a sudden, catastrophic descent and crashed into a South Florida neighborhood, leaving a massive crater and devastating families.
content:
A devastating private jet crash in South Florida has claimed the lives of all nine people on board, including a young family of four, their devoted caretaker, a couple, and a 20-year-old co-pilot.

The Learjet 60, bound for North Eleuthera in the Bahamas after taking off from Austin-Bergstrom International Airport in Texas, plummeted into a residential area in Greenacres, Florida, on Sunday afternoon. The high-speed impact created a massive crater and caused a massive fireball near the entrance of a mobile home park.

Victims Identified by Heartbroken Families

Grieving relatives released a joint statement on Monday identifying the seven passengers: Adam Robinson, 45, his wife Helen Sharp, 40, and their two young children, 4-year-old Emma and 2-year-old Charlie. Also killed were the family's caretaker, Anita Maria Cetina, and couple Rachael Reed and Charmi Fehr.

"Adam and Helen were devoted parents, and Emma and Charlie were the light of their lives," the family statement read. "Helen and Adam were the love affair that will last forever. Their warmth, generosity and gift for making people feel welcome touched so many lives."

The statement praised Cetina for showing a "legacy of unconditional love and devotion" while caring for the children, and described Reed and Fehr as "full of joy and adventure."

Among the two crew members lost was 20-year-old co-pilot Nathalia Filgueiras. Her mother shared that Filgueiras earned her pilot's license at 17 and had already logged more than 1,300 hours of flight time. Authorities have not yet publicly confirmed the identity of the second pilot or who was at the controls at the time of the crash.

Chilling Cockpit Audio and Fatal Descent

Federal investigators are examining weather conditions and flight data to determine what triggered the sudden catastrophe. According to the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) and air traffic control recordings, the flight crew reported atmospheric icing and moderate turbulence while cruising at 35,000 feet, prompting a request to climb to 37,000 feet to seek smoother air.

Moments later, the situation deteriorated rapidly. Audio recorded by LiveATC captured emergency Mayday calls as the jet went into an extreme dive, plunging initially at 10,000 feet per minute before descent rates spiked dramatically. Flightradar24 data indicated the vertical descent rate ultimately exceeded 32,000 feet per minute.

"We're going to crash into the ground," someone in the cockpit was heard saying, followed by the final transmission: "We're out of time."

Widespread Destruction and Federal Investigation

Eyewitness dashcam footage showed the aircraft diving out of the sky before exploding beside a roadway, narrowly missing surrounding homes. Debris damaged neighboring structures and injured a bystander's leg on the ground. Power was cut to the surrounding area, and local authorities evacuated roughly 600 residents to shelters as emergency teams contained the scene.

Florida Governor Ron DeSantis described the scene as a "cataclysmic plane crash," comparing the aircraft's rapid descent to a missile hitting the earth.

NTSB Senior Investigator Timothy Monville stated that recovery efforts would take several days, hampered by water accumulating inside the crash crater. NTSB officials also indicated that preliminary evidence suggests parts of the jet may have separated in mid-air prior to impact. Authorities have urged local residents who discover debris not to touch it and to immediately contact law enforcement or federal investigators.
